summary: saturn-bail ships Baileys fork with char-code-obfuscated exfiltration host in message-send path
details: lib/Socket/messages-send.js at lines 425 and 436 constructs a network destination via String.fromCharCode over a decimal-ASCII array that decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. The host is not a documented WhatsApp/Baileys endpoint and is hidden behind char-code obfuscation rather than appearing as a plain string, so the outbound call is not visible to a caller who reads the source normally. The obfuscation is wired into the socket's outbound message path, causing message/session-related data handled by the Baileys fork to be transmitted to a hardcoded third-party host each time messages are sent. This matches the pattern of covertly injected exfiltration in Baileys forks: an obfuscated destination inside a session-handling code path, no configurability, no documentation of the endpoint.
